title: Binance hack: developing story
summary: The largest crypto theft on record: attackers drained Binance hot wallets on several blockchains on Oct 29; about US$3 billion has been frozen, deposits work again, withdrawals are still paused and Binance says it is on track to resume them within about 45 hours, and it says it will cover the losses.

facts.label: Stolen
facts.note: Binance's own estimate of the impact (Reuters); Chainalysis's Jonathan Levin put it at US$6.4B in a later update (Cointelegraph, 05:01 UTC Oct 30); TRM Labs US$6.36B at the time taken
facts.source: Reuters via Investing.com; Cointelegraph live updates

facts.label: Frozen so far
facts.note: Binance said verified frozen assets reached US$3B (00:52 UTC Oct 30); Tether over US$1.567B USDT, Circle over US$800M USDC, First Digital froze the FDUSD involved

facts.label: Still with the attacker
facts.note: beyond the reach of issuers, per TRM Labs (as of 00:30 UTC Oct 30). These figures come from different sources and times (Binance for the total and the frozen amount, TRM Labs for this one), so stolen, frozen and still with the attacker need not add up

facts.label: Recovered
facts.note: frozen funds have not been reported as returned

facts.label: When
facts.note: most of it within about 20 minutes

facts.label: Who
facts.note: not confirmed by Binance or any government yet

facts.label: Binance
facts.value: deposits working normally; withdrawals still paused, 'on track' to resume in about 45 hours (as of Oct 30 morning); says it will cover all losses from its SAFU fund and company funds
facts.note: Preliminary finding: a compromised DevOps engineer's laptop let an attacker submit unauthorized withdrawals; Binance has since found 'additional points of breach' and CEO Richard Teng said it was not a one-click attack; no evidence of a private-key leak (Decrypt; Cointelegraph live updates, 08:37 UTC Oct 30). Binance.US not affected.
